brief: Tonight is Pull A — back, biceps, and your first deadlift in seventeen days. It is also your fifth training day in a row, so this card is built to be finished, not survived. The deadlift comes down. The app on its own would have reprinted 265 for six, three times; on 1 August you were asked for six at 265 and got four, five and five. Seventeen days and a ten-day gap later that is asking for reps you have never done on a bar you have not touched. So tonight is 225 for six to open, then 245 for six, three times. Six on all three and it goes to 255 next Pull A. The wide row gets its fourth set — you agreed to four back on 1 August and only three have ever made the log, so the step tonight is that set, not a heavier pin; 105 stays. Pulldown, dumbbell curls and hammer curls hold the same weights, but the rep targets are one above what you actually did last time instead of the top-of-range numbers the app keeps reprinting. Your two questions, both answered. Four sets of leg curls on RDL day: keep them. All four went 142.5 for twelve on 16 August with nothing falling off, in a thirty-six minute session, and the two lifts do different jobs — the RDL loads the hamstring at the hip, the curl loads it at the knee. And on correctives: you are right about what you have been seeing, and the exact picture is worse than it looks. Every upper-body corrective is gone — face pulls came off Pull A and Pull B on 1 August, Push B on 3 August and Push A on 14 August. The only two left in the whole program, hip adductor and hip abductor, sit on Legs A, and Legs A has not run since 2 August. There are four cards on your plan screen tonight: face pulls back on Pull A and Pull B, hip abductor onto Legs B, and the third rope pushdown set off Push A. Answer them at the gym. One thing I cannot put on a card: the angels and demons you did instead on 28 July have no matching exercise in the app at all — there is no shoulder-rotation and no anti-rotation movement in the list — so nobody can prescribe them to you until that list itself is changed. That needs your say-so, not a Yes/No tap. Conditioning: after a fifth straight lifting day, take a walk rather than anything hard.

dissent.progression: Drop the bar to 245 and keep four sets — 265 for six is a rep count he has never hit.
dissent.recovery: Keep 265 and drop the fourth set — three sets on a fifth straight day, weight untouched.
dissent.why: Both seats wanted less; they disagreed about which thing to spend. After seventeen days without a deadlift the risk sits in the heaviest bar on the card, not in the fourth set, and recovery's version keeps 265 — his top weight — on the bar twice on day five. Progression's caps the peak at 245, which is under what he already pulled that night, and asks for a rep count he can actually finish, which is also the only version that earns the next step before the block closes on 23 August. Recovery raised no pain or injury, so this was mine to call.

flags.note: Tonight is your fifth training day in a row. The card is cut to be finished — the deadlift is the only thing that changes much.
First deadlift in seventeen days, and it lands two days after RDLs at 205 and four sets of leg curls. That is why the bar comes down to 245 rather than back to 265.

Your leg-curl question, answered: four sets is right. All four went 142.5 for twelve on 16 August with nothing falling off, and the RDL loads the hamstring at the hip while the curl loads it at the knee.

Your corrective question, answered: every upper-body corrective is gone — face pulls came off all four days between 1 and 14 August. The only two left, hip adductor and hip abductor, are on Legs A, which has not run since 2 August. Four cards on your plan screen tonight offer to fix it.

Open, and I cannot card it: there is no shoulder-rotation and no anti-rotation movement anywhere in the app's exercise list, so your angels and demons cannot be prescribed until that list is changed. Say the word and it gets added.
Legs A has not run since 2 August — sixteen days. The rotation went Push A, Pull B, Legs B, Push A over the last four sessions.
On 17 August your overhead cable triceps 75 for twelve went on a substitute machine — you wrote that the cable was taken. That number is not a cable load and is not being read as one.
Meso 1 closes on 23 August and Meso 2 opens on the 24th. There is no back-off week in between.

proposals.why: Nothing corrective has been in front of you for over two weeks - face pulls came off all four days between 1 and 14 August, and the only two left, hip adductor and hip abductor, sit on Legs A, which you last logged on 2 August - so this puts three sets back on Pull A, your shortest session, as the only external-rotation movement in the program.
Pull B is the other day with no rear-shoulder or cuff work on it at all, and a second face-pull slot here means that cuff work lands twice a cycle instead of once.

Legs B is the only leg day with no hip work at all, and it is the day you hinge heavy, which is exactly where hip stability earns its keep - two sets of twelve to fifteen at 135, the weight you carried on 2 August, slotted after the leg curls.

The third set of rope pushdowns is the one that never holds - 14, 11 then 10 reps on 14 August, and on 17 August you dropped from 52.5 to 47.5 to finish it - so Push A ends on two hard sets instead of three at the tail of an eight-exercise day.

overrides.reason: Last time you pulled 225 for five, then 265 for four, five and five - the card asked for six on all four and you got six on none of them. That was seventeen days ago with ten days out of the gym since, so 245 for six is the bar tonight. Six on all three and it goes to 255 next Pull A.
Nine at 135, then eight and eight at 150 - the very bottom of the range, so 150 is not paid for yet. Same weights, one more rep than you actually did. When both 150 sets reach ten it moves to 157.5.

The one lift on this day that held up: eleven, twelve and eleven at 105 with nothing falling off. The step is the fourth set you agreed to on 1 August and have never logged, not a heavier pin - 105 stays while the extra set is new work.

Nine, nine and eight at the 30s last time - losing a rep by the end, not running out of range. The next dumbbell on the rack is 35, a five-pound jump in each hand, so it gets earned: ten, ten, ten at the 30s and it moves.
Eleven, eleven and ten at 42.5 - inside the range the whole way but never at the top of it. Hold 42.5; the cable has a small add-on weight, so twelve on all three only needs to move it to 43.75.
